title: Minimum Multiplicative Complexity of a Secure Block Cipher
summary: Prior efficiency-focused designs did not minimize multiplicative complexity; the minimum multiplication count for a secure block cipher remains unknown.

formal_statement.body: Earlier efforts toward low-multiplicative-complexity symmetric primitives focused on cost and performance under side-channel-attack countermeasures and did not minimize the multiplication count to the desired extent. In the Boolean-circuit model, with multiplicative complexity measured by the number of multiplications in $\mathrm{GF}(2)$, determine the minimum such number required to build a secure block cipher.

scope.domain: Design of secure block ciphers with low multiplicative complexity in Boolean circuits.
assumptions: The block cipher is represented in the Boolean-circuit model.
parameters: Number of multiplications in GF(2): the multiplicative-complexity measure to minimize
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the minimum number of GF(2) multiplications required to build a secure block cipher.

progress.summary: The source explicitly frames this as a motivating question after noting that prior side-channel-oriented work did not reduce multiplicative complexity far enough. It establishes neither a global minimum nor a matching lower bound.
citation_labels: Martin R. Albrecht et al., Ciphers for MPC and FHE
